geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Sort ad slogans ('If you drink Zoom, you'll run faster') into if-then form, then flip each one. Which flips are still believable?

  • I can write a conditional, its converse, inverse, and contrapositive.
  • I can write the converse, inverse and contrapositive of a conditional.
  • I can decide which of the four is true for a given statement, with a counterexample when false.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html: A conditional says 'if p, then q.' Swap the parts to get the converse: if q, then p. Put 'not' on both parts to get the inverse. Do both to get the contrapositive: if not q, then not p. A conditional and its contrapositive are always true or false together. The converse and the inverse are also always true or false together, but they can be false even when the original is true.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.html:
• conditional An if-then statement.
  • hypothesis The 'if' part of a conditional.
  • conclusion The 'then' part of a conditional.
  • converse Swap the if and then parts.
  • inverse Add 'not' to both parts.
  • contrapositive Swap the parts and add 'not' to both. It is true exactly when the original is.
  • truth table A chart that lists every true/false case for a statement.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.html:
Flip a statement four ways.

Read the worked steps
StepReason
P: 'it is a square.' Q: 'it is a rectangle.' The statement is 'if P, then Q.'Name the two parts.
Converse: if it is a rectangle, then it is a square.Swap P and Q.
Inverse: if it is not a square, then it is not a rectangle.Put 'not' on both parts.
Contrapositive: if it is not a rectangle, then it is not a square.Swap and put 'not' on both.
The original and the contrapositive mean the same thing. The converse is false: a 2 by 3 rectangle is not a square.One counterexample breaks the converse.
Second check: in the row with P false and Q true, the original is true but the converse is false.The truth table agrees.

Contrapositive: if it is not a rectangle, then it is not a square.
The original and the contrapositive mean the same thing. The converse is false: a 2 by 3 rectangle is not a square.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.html:
Which row breaks each statement?

Read the worked steps
StepReason
'If P, then Q' is false only when P is true and Q is false.That is the only way to break an if-then promise.
So 'if P, then Q' fails only in the row (T, F).Check each row.
'If Q, then P' fails only when Q is true and P is false: the row (F, T).Same rule, parts swapped.
Different rows break them, so swapping the parts changes when the statement is true.The converse is a different statement.
Second check: 'if P, then Q' means the same as 'not P, or Q.' Test the four rows with that.Same false row, found another way.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
Rae says 'If it's a square, it's a rectangle' is true, so 'If it's a rectangle, it's a square' must be true too.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Find and fix the error

That swap is the converse, and it needs its own check. A 2 by 3 rectangle is not a square.

slides.title: Practice 1
slides.html:
Statement: 'If a number is a multiple of 4, then it is even.' Write the converse, the inverse and the contrapositive.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Converse: if a number is even, then it is a multiple of 4. Inverse: if a number is not a multiple of 4, then it is not even. Contrapositive: if a number is not even, then it is not a multiple of 4. The original and the contrapositive match; the converse can fail.

Reveal second check

6 is even but not a multiple of 4, so the converse is false.

slides.title: Practice 2
slides.html:
Max says the negation (the 'not' version) of 'every marked angle is acute' is 'no marked angle is acute.' What is the correct negation? Show that Max's version can be wrong.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Correct opposite: at least one marked angle is not acute. With angles of 30 and 110 degrees, 'every angle is acute' is false, but 'no angle is acute' is also false.

Reveal second check

The 110 degree angle shows 'every' fails. The 30 degree angle shows 'none' fails.

slides.title: Practice 3
slides.html:
'If an integer is divisible by 6, then it is divisible by 3.' Find a counterexample to the converse and write the contrapositive.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Converse: if an integer is divisible by 3, then it is divisible by 6. The number 3 breaks it. Contrapositive: if an integer is not divisible by 3, then it is not divisible by 6. The original is true, because 6k = 3(2k).

Reveal second check

3 / 3 = 1, an integer. 3 / 6 = 1/2, not an integer.

geo.title: Practice 3
geo.prompt: 'If an integer is divisible by 6, then it is divisible by 3.' Find a counterexample to the converse and write the contrapositive.
geo.solution: Converse: if an integer is divisible by 3, then it is divisible by 6. The number 3 breaks it. Contrapositive: if an integer is not divisible by 3, then it is not divisible by 6. The original is true, because 6k = 3(2k).
